mathematical_context: Concrete additive subgroup kernel of a homomorphism of abelian groups
mathematical_reason: ProofWiki directly defines kernels for group homomorphisms as inverse images of the group identity; additive notation gives 0_B for abelian groups. The subgroup is a concrete set of elements, while the associated categorical kernel is an inclusion arrow with a universal property. The two are related but not literally the same object data.

mathematical_context: Universal-property kernel of a morphism in a preadditive category, existence conditional
mathematical_reason: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 1 gives an arrow satisfying annihilation and unique universal factorization; item 2 explicitly uses conditional 'if the kernel exists'. A preadditive category need not have all kernels. The definition is a morphism universal property, not a bare subset of a domain.

mathematical_context: Universal-property cokernel of a morphism in a preadditive category, existence conditional
mathematical_reason: Stacks Definition 12.3.9 item 3 supplies the dual universal property and item 4 explicitly qualifies notation by existence. In the category of abelian groups the corresponding morphism may be modeled by projection onto B/im(f), but the definition does not presuppose that all preadditive categories possess cokernels.

mathematical_context: Complex exact at interior objects of an abelian category, where images and kernels exist
mathematical_reason: Stacks Definition 12.5.7 first defines a complex using zero composites in an additive category, then imposes image-equals-kernel exactness only after assuming an abelian category. Short exact sequences include zero objects at both ends. In arbitrary preadditive or merely additive categories the image/kernels may fail to exist, so this strong exactness claim cannot be transported there.
